label: Workato api token
name: workato_api_token
hint: Workato Data Tables API token. Needed on a press of a real game (never of a test game), and on the typed-word recipe so that typing the word again can find the game the person already runs or plays in. Without it on the typed recipe the word always opens the setup card.

label: Slack bot token
name: slack_bot_token
hint: Bot token. Scopes: chat:write and users:read; channels:read (groups:read in a private channel) for Everyone in this channel; channels:history (groups:history) for test games only; im:write as a fallback for private messages.

label: Text
name: text
hint: [typed] The Slack message text. A message with itambola or ihousie in it is the word; anything else is skipped. Leave it empty on the click recipe.

label: User ID
name: user_id
hint: [both] Slack id of whoever typed the word [typed] or pressed the control [click].

label: Channel
name: channel
hint: [both] Channel id the message [typed] or the button [click] is in. A ticket press arrives from the player's private message, so there it is that message's channel; the game's own channel is read from the game.

label: Message ts
name: message_ts
hint: [typed] ts of the message that holds the word. The game's id is made from it, so one typed word is one game.

label: Thread ts
name: thread_ts
hint: [typed] Parent ts if the word was typed in a thread. The setup card then appears in that thread; a top-level word gets its card in the channel.

label: Bot user ID
name: bot_user_id
hint: [typed] The bot's own user id, so it never starts a game for itself.

label: Subtype
name: subtype
hint: [typed] Slack message subtype. Edits, joins and so on are skipped.

label: Bot ID
name: bot_id
hint: [typed] Present on bot messages -- skipped.

label: Payload
name: payload
hint: [click] The whole interaction payload as JSON text (map the trigger's block_actions object in formula mode with .to_json). With it the click recipe needs nothing else but the two tokens: the user, channel, message, button, menu picks, response_url and the size dropdown's current choice (state) are all read from it. The trigger's own {"block_actions:button": {...}} wrapper is fine. Anything mapped by hand in the fields below is kept; the payload only fills what is blank. Leave it empty on the typed recipe.

label: Action value
name: action_value
hint: [click] The pressed button's value (actions[0].value): tb|<kind>|<game>|<arg> for a real game, tbt|<kind>|<json> for a test game. Its presence (or action_id's) is what makes this call a click instead of the typed word. Not needed when payload is mapped. Leave it empty on the typed recipe.

label: Action ID
name: action_id
hint: [click] actions[0].action_id. Needed for the organizer's player menu, which has no value: its action_id is tambola_click_pick_<game>. Harmless on every other press.

label: Selected users
name: selected_users
hint: [click] actions[0].selected_users: the people chosen on the organizer's player menu when it is Slack's people picker (used when the channel has more people than the channel's own list can hold). A list or text; Slack user ids are picked out of whatever arrives. Leave it empty if absent.

label: Selected options
name: selected_options
hint: [click] actions[0].selected_options: the people chosen on the organizer's player menu when it is the channel's own list (a list of {text, value} options; only the values, Slack user ids, are read). Map it next to selected_users: the menu is the channel's list unless the channel has more people than one menu holds, when it is Slack's people picker and its picks arrive in selected_users. Leave it empty if absent.

label: State
name: state
hint: [click] The interaction's state (top level, next to actions): what every dropdown on the message shows right now. Only for mapping field by field: the setup card's Game size, Board style and Winners dropdowns are read from it when a way of joining is pressed. Not needed when payload is mapped. Leave it empty if absent.

label: Source ts
name: source_ts
hint: [click] ts of the message that holds the button (container.message_ts). For a ticket press it is the ticket message, which is redrawn.

label: Action ts
name: action_ts
hint: [click] Slack's own click time (actions[0].action_ts). A prize goes to the earliest click, a second Next number within about a second of the last is taken as a double press, and a menu pick processed late is told from a newer one by it.

label: Response URL
name: response_url
hint: [click] The press's response_url (the top-level response_url of the interaction payload, not inside actions). Optional but recommended: with it the organizer's private controls are UPDATED IN PLACE, one note for the whole game (Start turns the lobby's controls into the game's, each Next number shows what was just called, Review and Resume swap the buttons, a stale button turns into the right ones), instead of a new private note each time the game moves on. Only Slack's own response URLs are used; anything else is ignored with a warning.

label: Testing
name: testing
hint: "yes" for a test game: the lobby, board, tickets and controls are all real and work, but nothing is written to the data table. The game is kept in the messages it posts (the bot needs channels:history, or groups:history, to read them back). Set it on the typed-word recipe only: later presses recognise a test game by its buttons.

label: Skip post
name: skip_post
hint: "yes" to post nothing and write nothing: the cards come back in preview_json (paste a "blocks" list into Slack's Block Kit Builder).

label: Announce
name: announce
hint: [typed] Where a won prize is announced: channel (the default), thread (a reply under the board) or off. The board shows who holds each prize either way.

label: Prizes
name: prizes
hint: [typed] Comma separated prizes in play, from early5, top, middle, bottom, full (early five, top line, full house and so on also work). Blank = all five.

label: Board columns
name: board_columns
hint: [typed] Squares in a row of the board, 3 to 10. Default 10, the traditional nine rows. 5 gives eighteen shorter rows, kinder to a phone.

label: Max players
name: max_players
hint: [typed] Most players a game holds. Default 60, never more than 100. Each player costs a table write and a private message, and a Workato Python step is stopped at 90 seconds.

label: Size
name: size
hint: [typed] The game size the setup card's Game size dropdown opens on: small (numbers 1 to 30, 9 on a ticket: a quick game), medium (1 to 60, 12 on a ticket) or large (1 to 90, 15 on a ticket: the classic game). Blank = large. The organizer chooses the size on that dropdown, which is what counts; this only sets where it starts, for a channel that mostly plays quick games.

label: Top N
name: top_n
hint: [typed] Players the Review ranks, 1 to 50. Default 10. The review is a short table of the players with the most numbers marked, then a count of the rest, so a hundred players still make one short card.

label: Board style
name: board_style
hint: [typed] The board style the setup card's Board style dropdown opens on: emoji (a square for every number, number emojis where called: the default), numbers (a plain grid with ?? for each number until it is called) or list (just the numbers called so far). Blank = emoji. The organizer chooses on the dropdown, which is what counts; this only sets where it starts.

label: Winners style
name: winners_style
hint: [typed] The winners display the setup card's Winners dropdown opens on: names (who holds each prize, in a list on the board: the default), carousel (a Slack carousel card for each winner with their profile picture, the first winner on the right and each new one added to the left), strip (small profile pictures in one line) or none. The carousel or strip is the board's winners list: it is hidden until the organizer presses Show winners (and Hide winners takes it off again). In a photo style each prize's announcement also shows the person who has just won on a small card (their profile photo on top, then the prize, their name and the numbers that made the line), after the banner, until the next number is called. The Show winners / Hide winners button appears on the organizer's controls once somebody has won. Blank = names. The organizer chooses on the dropdown, which is what counts; this only sets where it starts. If Slack refuses the carousel the board shows names instead.

label: Banners
name: banners
hint: [click] Optional pictures that open the announcement of a prize, as a JSON object of public https image addresses, as text: {"early5": "https://.../early-five.png", "top": "https://.../top-line.png", "middle": "https://.../middle-line.png", "bottom": "https://.../bottom-line.png", "full": "https://.../full-house.png"}. In a photo winners style the winner's own profile photo follows the banner, on a small card with the prize, their name and the numbers that made the line. Pressing Next number deletes the announcements of the prizes won since the number before (where the board lists winners; with the none style each stays as its plain line, as the only record); Full House's stays up for celebration_seconds when the game ends, and is then cleared with every other announcement. Name only the prizes that have one; "lines" gives all three lines one picture. Set it as a fixed value on the click recipe, where prizes are won. A bad address or prize name is left out and listed in warnings, and a picture Slack cannot load is left out too: the announcement still goes. Without it the announcement is its header and emojis. Make Full House the tallest.

label: Celebration seconds
name: celebration_seconds
hint: [click] How long Full House's celebration (its announcement, banner and winner's card) stays up before the game's screen is cleared: when Full House ends the game, the job waits this many seconds, then deletes the announcements, leaving the board with its final winners list. Default 20, 0 clears it at once, never more than 60 (a Workato step is stopped at 90 seconds). Set it as a fixed value on the click recipe.
